notes: Fifteen markets of the first real build whose three facets a reader can check by eye, with the facets CONTRACTS_V2 7.14's tagger must give them and the reason for each. The expectations are written out rather than computed, so an edit to tags.v1.json or to kalshi_series_facets.v1.json that moves one of them fails a test instead of moving a cohort. Every row carries only the eight fields the tagger may read.

market.question: Will BTC trimmed mean be above $80000.00 by 11:59 PM ET on Apr 30, 2026? (Above $80,000.00)

cases.why: The sealed series map answers KXBTCMAXMON and the question's own 'above' decides the structure.

market.question: Will BTC trimmed mean be below $60000.00 by 11:59 PM ET on Aug 31, 2026? (Below $60,000.00)

cases.why: The same series and the same subject with the opposite threshold: the structure is the question's.

market.question: Will the gold close price be above 4344.99 USD/t.oz on August 07, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT? (Above $4344.99)

cases.why: The boundary case: KXGOLDW is the weekly gold series and this leg's life is exactly seven days, which is the month bucket because the week bucket is strictly below 7 d. The horizon is the market's own life, not the cadence of its series and not the word August in it.

market.question: Will the President's approval rating be between 39.1 and 39.3 according to RealClearPolitics? (39.1 to 39.3)

cases.why: A range ladder leg: two numbers joined by 'and' beat the 'above' rule because range-band is first.

market.question: Will there be more than 25 tornadoes in November? (Above 25)

cases.why: A count of events over a month, not a threshold on a price, and the series names the subject.

market.question: Snow in Dallas in Jan 2026? (Above 2.0 inches)

cases.why: The series map cannot tell snow from temperature from 'Dallas, Weather forecasting', so it is absent and the question's own 'snow' decides: this is the worked example of ruling R295.

market.question: Will the average temperature in Austin be above 90°F for 4 or more consecutive days in the week of Aug 18, 2026? (4+ consecutive days)

cases.why: Consecutive days above a temperature is a count over a period, and the subject is the question's.

market.question: What will be the top AI model this month? (gemini-2.5-pro)

cases.why: The ticker fixes the structure here: one leg of a multi-outcome event, which the question's own wording ('What will be the top') would also reach.

market.question: Will  Aug 2025 be the hottest Aug ever? (Hottest ever)

cases.why: One dated leg of a recurring climate benchmark, which is neither a threshold nor a comparison.

market.question: Will this market be above 50% when it closes?

cases.why: Self-referential by its question: platform-meta is first in precedence, so it wins outright.

market.question: Will Russia and Ukraine agree to a ceasefire before August 1, 2026?

cases.why: An event by a date. The horizon is the 131-day life, not the 'August 1, 2026' in the text.

market.question: Will Starship flight 12 happen before New Glenn flight 3?

cases.why: Two flights raced against each other: head-to-head, decided before the by-date rule.

market.question: Will Hearts win the Scottish league?

cases.why: A contest with a winner. The ten-day life is a month horizon, which is the boundary at 7 days.

market.question: Will I walk 500k steps in October?

cases.why: The reported tail: a personal goal the vocabulary does not name, counted as other on both facets rather than forced into a subject.
Not self-referential by its two words: it is platform-meta only because the provider labelled it nonpredictive, which is the half of decision D-S14's reconciliation the keyword rule misses.
